clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old previously healthy male presented with a 9-month progressive multisystem illness characterized by watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss of 6 kg, nocturnal fever, multiple cutaneous ulcers with necrotic crust, painful erythematous nodules on lower limbs, glans ulcers with fibrinous floor, and oligoarthritis of small joints. Colonoscopy revealed multiple shallow ulcers in the sigmoid colon and proximal rectum. Initial TB screening (tuberculin skin test and chest X-ray) was negative. Histopathological examination of a lower limb ulcer biopsy demonstrated epithelioid granulomatous process with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis. Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) staining by Ziehl-Neelsen method showed intact bacilli, and mycobacterial culture was positive for M. tuberculosis, confirming the diagnosis of cutaneous TB. Gastrointestinal biopsy showed only mild inflammatory infiltrate without bacilli, indicating primary cutaneous TB rather than disseminated disease.
